subject: math
title: 4 questions from earlier lessons
instructions: Work every problem on paper first and show each step. Then type your answer and press Check. You get two tries on each question. Type a fraction like 3/4, a mixed number like 2 1/2, and a power like 3^4.

sections.name: Catch-up
sections.desc: Questions you missed before, with new numbers or a new story. Right on the first try takes one off your list.

items.q: A bakery needs help packing boxes for 7 days before a holiday, and it offers your scout troop two ways to be paid. Plan A pays $160 every day. Plan B pays $9 on day 1, and the pay doubles every day after that: day 2 pays $18, day 3 pays $36, and so on.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Total pay for the 7 days under Plan A

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Pay on day 7 alone under Plan B

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Total pay for the 7 days under Plan B

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Which plan should the troop take for these 7 days?

ans.model: Plan A pays $1,120 in total. Plan B pays $1,143 in total, so Plan B pays $23 more. Plan B starts far behind and only passes Plan A's total on the last day.
ans.look: Names both totals ($1,120 and $1,143) and says how much more Plan B pays ($23).

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Give the reason for your choice. Name both totals and say how much more the better plan pays.

a: b) Double each day: 9, 18, 36, 72, 144, 288, 576. Day 7 pays $576.
d) and e) Decision: Plan B, because $1,143 is more than $1,120.
items.hint: Write the day numbers 1 to 7 in a row and the pay under each one. Add the pay in pairs, then add the whole row a second time to check.

items.q: A swim club books a pool party: 2 coaches pay $14 each and 26 swimmers pay $6 each. The pool gives $16 off the total. Jon writes the cost as (2 × 14 + 26) × 6 − 16. Rosa writes it as 2 × 14 + 26 × 6 − 16.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Whose expression matches the real cost of the party?

options: No, the club needs more money

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The club has collected $175. Is that enough to pay for the party?

ans.model: The coaches cost 2 × 14 = $28 and the swimmers cost 26 × 6 = $156. After the $16 off, the party costs $168, which is the value of Rosa's expression. Jon's parentheses multiply the coaches' cost by 6 as well, so his total is far too high. $175 is $7 more than $168, so the club has enough with $7 left over.
ans.look: Says the party costs $168, says that Jon's parentheses multiply the coaches' $28 by 6 too, and says $7 is left over.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Give the reason for your two choices. Write three things: the real cost, what the parentheses in the wrong expression change, and how much money is left over.

a: c) Rosa's expression matches, because each coach pays $14 once and each swimmer pays $6 once.
d) 175 − 168 = 7, so $175 is enough and $7 is left over.
e) Decision: use Rosa's expression. The party costs $168, and $175 covers it with $7 to spare.
items.hint: In Rosa's expression, do both multiplications before you add or subtract. In Jon's, finish the parentheses first. For the reason, check that you wrote all three things.

items.q: Add the odd numbers in order, starting from 1, and look at the sums: 1 = 1, 1 + 3 = 4 and 1 + 3 + 5 = 9.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write your answer to part a as a power with exponent 2. Type it with the ^ key.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the pattern to find the sum of the first 14 odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 and so on up to 27.

a: b) There are 11 odd numbers in part a, and 121 = 11 × 11 = 11².
c) Count the odd numbers from 1 to 27: (27 + 1) ÷ 2 = 14, so there are 14 of them.
14² = 196, so adding the first 14 odd numbers gives 196.
items.hint: Compare each sum with how many odd numbers were added to make it. Before part c, check on paper how many odd numbers run from 1 to 27.

items.q: A robotics club tests a computer program that builds a list. The list doubles in length every second. After 1 second it has 2 items, after 2 seconds it has 4 items, and after 3 seconds it has 8 items.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many items are in the list after 9 seconds?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: After how many seconds does the list have more than 6,000 items for the first time?

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: After 17 seconds the list has 2¹⁷ items. Seventeen 2s multiplied together is the same as seven 2s times ten 2s, which is 2⁷ × 2¹⁰. Find the value of 2¹⁷.

a: a) 2⁹ = 512, so the list has 512 items after 9 seconds.
2¹³ = 8,192, which is more than 6,000, so the first time is after 13 seconds.
items.hint: For part c, find 2⁷ and 2¹⁰ first, then multiply them in two pieces and add. Check each digit before you type it.
